entries.answer: Use axes or chainsaws to fell trees and control the fall direction: first observe the species, lean and crown bias, surrounding obstacles, and weather, and clear the work area and escape route; determine the position and depth of the undercut and back cut based on the judgment, and drive wedges or use jacks to control the fall direction when necessary; shut down and withdraw to a safe position when the tree falls, then buck, limb, and mark to specification, verify length and quality, and maintain a sharpened chainsaw and related equipment.
entries.question: What do fallers mainly do?

entries.answer: This occupation faces standing trees directly and centers on fall-direction judgment, notch work, and escape safety; skidding and transport machine operation focuses on log loading and hauling, sawmill workers on log sawing and processing, tree trimmers on pruning and maintaining standing trees, and forest and conservation workers on forest tending and patrol. These positions often collaborate on the same work face, but their tasks and responsibilities differ and they cannot substitute for one another.

ILO research in 2023 shows that task exposure differs greatly across occupations, and tasks centered on on-site operations and safety responsibility usually have a lower share of high exposure; technical feasibility does not mean institutions have already adopted it. The conclusion is that the way of working will change, not that the occupation will be wholly replaced.

entries.answer: No. The median is the midpoint of the wage distribution of workers in the same statistical period, not a starting wage; this page did not obtain the officially published 25th and 75th percentiles, which are kept as gaps and not filled in. The 10th and 90th percentiles are about 35,180 and 82,360 USD/year respectively (presented via the US Department of Labor-funded My Next Move). This occupation is strongly affected by season and weather, and individual income depends on the work method, pay definitions, and region.

entries.answer: The 2025 median annual wage is 52,100 USD (median hourly 25.05 USD, BLS OEWS, presented via O*NET); the 10th and 90th percentiles are about 35,180 and 82,360 USD/year respectively (presented via the US Department of Labor-funded My Next Move), and the 25th and 75th percentiles and by-industry wages were not obtained this time and are kept as gaps rather than filled in. Employment in 2024 was about 5,600, a decline is projected for 2024—2034 (-1% or lower), and about 700 job openings are projected.

entries.answer: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), SVP below 6.0; the education survey shows that some positions require a high school diploma or equivalent, some accept less than high school, and some require a postsecondary certificate (the complete percentage distribution was not obtained this time). The US usually requires a high school equivalent and provides on-the-job training, with safety training per the employer's and regulatory requirements. Mainland China usually requires junior high or above with position and safety training, subject to the employer and the job posting.

entries.answer: Work must be carried out with protective equipment provided and used per forestry work safety procedures (leg protection, helmet, hearing and eye and face protection), and chainsaws and other equipment must be inspected and maintained per the rules; the tree and surroundings must be observed and the escape route cleared before work, and work must stop when weather or tree conditions are unfavorable. The O*NET work context shows that about 68% of respondents have work arrangements described as irregular (changing with weather, production needs, or contract periods) and that errors at work have serious consequences. The above must be verified against the employer's and the regulations' original text; this section does not replace safety procedures or legal requirements.
entries.question: What safety and protection requirements are there?

entries.answer: The main risks are a wrong fall-direction judgment or improper notch causing the tree to go out of control, falling dead limbs and dangerous trees, chainsaw kickback or equipment failure, an uncleared work area and escape route, and the combined risk of weather changes and fatigue. The boundaries are: the work must be performed by trained personnel per procedures, and dangerous trees, severe crown bias, or unfavorable weather require stopping and reporting; this page provides no safe operating or legal advice.
entries.question: What risks and boundaries does the work have?

entries.answer: Employment in 2024 was about 5,600, a decline is projected for 2024—2034 (-1% or lower), and about 700 job openings are projected (mainly from replacement demand); this trend does not break out an AI adoption variable. A transition usually requires adding safety procedures and equipment operation capability: people from a forestry or landscape background need mechanical work and safety procedures, and people from a mechanical background need species characteristics, forest land work organization, and safety requirements.

paragraphs: FermatMind career content research process

This round checked O*NET45-4021 tasks, context, and education, the complete NationalWages2025 five tiers, the BLS2025—2035 exact projections, and the NBS2025 agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery pre-tax annual average; ILO WP96/NIST1.0 reuses materials already read in the same round and is not forestry law.
2026-10-11 (author verification of the nine modules this round)

The 2025 US national quintiles and the 2025—2035 exact projections were obtained, and the assertion that the 25th and 75th percentiles are unpublished was withdrawn. Precise US by-industry wages, Chinese occupational and city wages and current representative recruitment, complete forestry jurisdictional rules and training period and cost, occupational AI adoption benefit causation, personality performance, and accident control effects still lack evidence. The current O*NET education data show only three categories for some positions, with no percentages, and none are invented. China's agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery 74,424/46,552 is a pre-tax annual broad industry average. Legacy periods, percentile gaps, and safety narratives in the FAQ and shared register are preserved under protection; the exercise answers, works, and seven-day materials are unchanged and not independently accepted.

subject.summary: Use axes or chainsaws to fell trees, controlling the fall direction per species characteristics and cutting technique and reducing tree damage; this includes judging tree lean and tilt direction, determining the notch position and depth, driving wedges or using jacks to control the fall direction, clearing the work area and escape routes, bucking logs to specification and verifying quality and length, and maintaining chainsaws and related equipment; the work assumes on-site safety and operating procedures.
